name: Douglas A-26 Invader
summary: Fast twin-engine WWII attack bomber that also flew in Korea and Vietnam; a dozen fly in private hands, some in glazed-nose or gun-nose configuration.

engines: Two R-2800 radial engines in big round cowls with three or four-blade propellers
Engines carried at the leading edge of the wing
fuselage: Slim, streamlined fuselage with a bubble canopy over the pilots
Glazed bombardier nose (A-26C) or solid nose with machine guns (A-26B)
tail: Single tall fin with a large squared rudder
Horizontal tail mounted on the fuselage

tellTales: Slim twin-radial bomber with a single tall tail and a bubble canopy
Mid-set wing and a tricycle-gear stance on a twin-engine attack bomber
Glazed or gun nose on a clean, sleek fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The B-25 has twin fins and a gull wing; the A-26 has one tall fin and a straight wing.
The Tracker is a high-wing with a fat fuselage; the A-26 is a mid-wing with a slim fuselage.
The Beech 18 is much smaller with twin fins and tailwheel gear; the A-26 has a single tall fin and tricycle gear.
The DC-3 is a low-wing airliner with tailwheel gear; the A-26 is a sleek attack bomber with tricycle gear.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
